## What is oma?

**oma** (Open Managed Agents) is the infrastructure layer for AI agents. You bring the harness — the loop that decides what the model does next — and oma takes care of everything else: durable sessions, sandboxed code execution, tool calls, semantic memory, secret-safe credentials, and crash recovery.

It runs entirely on Cloudflare (Workers, Durable Objects, D1, R2, KV, Vectorize, Containers), and you can either use the **hosted product at [oma.duyet.net](https://app.oma.duyet.net)** or **fork and self-host** to your own Cloudflare account.

## Why oma?

Most agent frameworks tell you *how* to build an agent — the loop, the prompt format, the orchestration shape. oma is different: it stays out of the harness and instead provides what every long-running agent needs but is painful to build.

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Durable sessions" icon="approve-check">
    Append-only event log per session in a SQLite-backed Durable Object. Resume from anywhere; survive restarts and crashes.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Sandboxed execution" icon="seti:docker">
    Tool calls run in per-session Cloudflare Containers. Pre-install Python / Node / apt packages declaratively.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Vault-backed credentials" icon="seti:lock">
    Secrets never enter the sandbox. An outbound proxy injects auth headers per-host so tools can hit private APIs without ever seeing the key.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Built-in memory" icon="document">
    Per-agent semantic memory across sessions, indexed in Vectorize via Workers AI embeddings.
  </Card>
  <Card title="MCP, everywhere" icon="puzzle">
    Connect any MCP server and oma auto-generates `mcp_*` tools the model can call.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Three integrations, day one" icon="rocket">
    Publish agents into Linear (assignable issues), GitHub (PRs), and Slack (channels) with OAuth-managed auth.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Sandbox platforms

Every sandbox — cloud container, local process, or browser tab — runs behind one `SandboxExecutor` interface, selected per-environment via `sandbox_provider`. Availability differs between the Cloudflare deployment and self-host Node; see the [Kubernetes deploy guide](/deploy/kubernetes/) and [k8s-bridge reference](/deploy/k8s-bridge/) for the cluster-backed options.

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Cloud" icon="cloudflare">
    Cloudflare Containers (default on Cloudflare) · BoxRun · Kubernetes via k8s-remote or OpenShell (both runtimes, gateway-relayed on Cloudflare) · Daytona and E2B (self-host Node only) · Dynamic Workers — ephemeral V8-isolate JS/Wasm eval, Cloudflare only · oma-remote federation to another oma instance (Cloudflare; Node not yet wired)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Local" icon="seti:docker">
    Local subprocess via `oma bridge daemon` (both runtimes — relayed to Cloudflare over WebSocket) · Docker / `docker-compose` (self-host Node) · Kubernetes pods, direct in-cluster (self-host Node) · LiteBox micro-VMs (self-host Node)
  </Card>
  <Card title="Browser" icon="seti:html">
    Browser VM — a WASM VM (v86) running inside a browser tab, paired as a runtime and driven over the same relay as the local subprocess provider. Zero-infra sandboxing for demos and constrained environments.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Model providers

Bring your own model or credentials — an agent references a model by id, and oma resolves credentials per tenant.

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Anthropic" icon="approve-check">
    Direct API access with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — the default provider fallback when no Model Card matches.
  </Card>
  <Card title="OpenAI-compatible" icon="random">
    Any `/chat/completions`-compatible endpoint via a Model Card (`oai` / `oai-compatible`).
  </Card>
  <Card title="AnyRouter" icon="puzzle">
    One-click OAuth connect from the Console — no pasted key. Auto-provisions model cards (e.g. `anyrouter/free`, `anyrouter-strong`, `anyrouter-fast`) with a live credit balance and preset picker.
  </Card>
  <Card title="poolside" icon="rocket">
    The `laguna` / `malibu` agentic-coding models, driven through the `poolside` harness over the same OpenAI-compatible loop.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Custom Model Cards / BYOK" icon="seti:lock">
    Per-tenant credentials with a custom `base_url`, for any Anthropic-wire or OpenAI-wire provider you self-host or proxy.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Harnesses

The harness decides *how* an agent's turn runs; the platform decides *what* it has available (tools, skills, sandbox, history). oma ships two harnesses today, with more planned:

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="OMA harness (default)" icon="document">
    oma's own agent loop, built on the [`ai` SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/) — prompt-cache-safe context engineering, tool loop, and event emission. Works out of the box for any agent.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Claude Agent SDK" icon="seti:lock">
    Runs the actual Claude Code CLI as a subprocess (self-host Node only), with per-agent model and credential resolution via Model Cards.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Local runtime (ACP bridge)" icon="seti:docker">
    `acp-proxy` delegates the whole loop to a local [ACP](https://agentclientprotocol.com/)-compatible agent — Claude Code, Codex — running on a paired machine via `oma bridge daemon`.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

More harnesses are planned — see [Architecture](/architecture/) for how to implement and register your own.
